objectives: Distinguish a store's power (MW) from its energy (MWh) and calculate its duration
Calculate round-trip efficiency by multiplying the efficiency of each step
Compare batteries, pumped hydro and hydrogen by duration, efficiency and best use

questions.prompt: A battery is rated 200 MW / 800 MWh. What can it do when full?
choices: Deliver 800 MWh every hour for 4 hours
questions.explain: Power (200 MW) is how fast it can discharge and energy (800 MWh) is how much it holds, so at full power it lasts 800 ÷ 200 = 4 hours. Its power rating caps it at 200 MW, so it cannot deliver 800 MW, however briefly.

questions.prompt: A hydrogen store uses an electrolyser that keeps 70 %, compression and storage that keep 90 %, and a fuel cell that keeps 50 %. What is the round-trip efficiency?
choices: 70 %, the average of the three steps
questions.explain: Losses multiply: 0.70 × 0.90 × 0.50 = 0.315, so about 32 % comes back, close to the Department of Energy baseline of 31 %. Averaging, or looking only at the weakest step, ignores that each step works on what the step before has left.

questions.prompt: An upper reservoir holds 2 million m³ of water 250 m above the lower one. About how much electricity comes back if the plant recovers 80 %?
questions.explain: E = 1,000 × 2 × 10⁶ × 9.81 × 250 ≈ 4.9 × 10¹² J, about 1,360 MWh stored, and 80 % of that is about 1,090 MWh. 1,360 MWh forgets the losses, and 1,700 MWh divides by 0.8 instead of multiplying.

questions.prompt: Hydrogen returns only about 31 % of the electricity put in. Why is it still studied as a store for the grid?
choices: It answers within a second, faster than a battery
It can store energy for weeks or seasons, which no battery can do cheaply
It already holds more than 90 % of the world's stored electricity
It has the lowest installed cost per kWh in the page's table
questions.explain: Hydrogen's strength is size and time: a salt cavern of it can hold energy for weeks or seasons. Batteries answer in about a second but are economical for hours, not weeks, and the store holding more than 90 % of the world's stored electricity is pumped hydro.
